purpose: Three simplified style previews for copper in L1 earth, each with a small illustrative thumbnail. Not an implemented or finalized seamless tileset; thumbnails are not measured gameplay captures.

variants.name: 1-kantig
variants.description: Variant 1: THREE ANGULAR COPPER CHUNKS, clean geometric fractured metal forms. One large asymmetric chunk, two smaller chunks beside it, each only 3 broad polygon faces. Crisp graphic game sprite, warm orange-copper, dark umber shadows and restrained peach highlights. Earthen rim broken into a few simple angular shapes. Very clear silhouette, very low detail.
variants.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a very SIMPLE low-detail 2D copper ore terrain TILE design for a mining game, L1 brown earth. This is a readability prototype at small game scale, NOT realistic concept art. Think a hand-drawn 64-by-64 sprite enlarged for inspection: broad clean shapes, deliberately chunky edges, at most EIGHT solid colors total for copper, soil, highlights and shadows. Absolutely no tiny noise, no gritty texture, no grain, no photographic detail, no intricate cracks, no hundreds of pebbles, no brushstroke microtexture. Straight-on orthographic terrain plane, no isometric block or perspective cube. Only TWO TO FOUR clearly distinguishable large copper masses, orange-brown solid metallic copper with one broad pale-copper highlight plane and one dark brown plane on each piece. Copper partially buried in dull brown soil; just a NARROW irregular earth overlap and a short dark contact shadow, no deep cavity, no high sidewalls. Earth has a handful of big understated brown clod shapes, lower contrast than the copper. The ore occupies roughly half the tile, all four square tile edges are soil. No gemstone spikes, transparent crystals, lava, glow, sparks, text, labels, numbers, UI or people. PRESENTATION: a plain dark charcoal background, one large SQUARE TILE preview on the left and an identical much smaller thumbnail on the right about one seventh its width, aligned at their centers. The thumbnail is the SAME tile design so the user can see small-scale readability. Only these two renditions of the same tile, no extra examples. Large tile and thumbnail both opaque earth squares, no ornamental frame. Landscape image. Variant 1: THREE ANGULAR COPPER CHUNKS, clean geometric fractured metal forms. One large asymmetric chunk, two smaller chunks beside it, each only 3 broad polygon faces. Crisp graphic game sprite, warm orange-copper, dark umber shadows and restrained peach highlights. Earthen rim broken into a few simple angular shapes. Very clear silhouette, very low detail.

variants.name: 2-flache-ader
variants.description: Variant 2: A FLAT WINDING COPPER SEAM, made from TWO connected broad irregular copper plates plus ONE small separate fragment. Copper sits almost flush with the earth, short branching bends and a thin dark edge imply embedding. Broad flatter painterly shapes, 3 tones for copper, large uninterrupted middle-color planes with only 2-3 restrained highlight facets. Simple compact sprite, no rock pile.

variants.name: 3-rund
variants.description: Variant 3: THREE ROUNDED IRREGULAR COPPER NUGGETS, chunky friendly stylized shapes. One large nugget and two smaller nuggets embedded in softly shaped dirt clods. Broad cartoon painted shading using only 3 solid color regions on each nugget, mildly angular highlights to retain metallic material. Clean uncluttered, no outline stroke, no fine surface detail.
